system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Draft (SPA and Disclosure Letter)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point, and I recommend rejecting it as the base document. Three points shape the response:

- **The "[STANDARD]" and "FINAL" labels don't bind us.** The Seller asks us to skip anything not marked [OPEN]. Every clause that matters departs from our playbook, so the labels cannot clear them. The "market" statements (10-20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12-18 month limits) are unsupported assertions and do not override our positions.
- **There is no authority for the Seller's package.** The Seller says the terms were "settled at principal level." Nothing in our file shows Amelia Frost approved them. Under the playbook, the 20% cap and 18-month period are conditional fallbacks that require her prior written authority identifying the draft. None has been given. We should confirm with her directly that no one on the deal team has indicated acceptance.
- **Several items go to whether the deal is safe to complete.** These are Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses in the funds flow, title, and the privacy incident. They need conditions precedent or price mechanics, not just drafting changes.

## Issue-by-issue comparison

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (start). 20% only as fallback with Amelia Frost's written authority | Open at 25% / 6m. Do not concede 20% |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. Counter at 5,000 |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Counter at 50k tipping basket |
| General time limit (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only as fallback with authority) | Counter at 24 months |
| Cross-application of limits | Limits apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. Limits apply only to General Warranty Claims |
| Fundamental/Title | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap; at least 6 years; outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to all Claims "of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of them, to the maximum extent enforceable, non-waivable | Reject. Add express carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1-1.2) | General disclosure of entire data room, Accounts and public registers | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room and register deemed disclosure | Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2 |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Blanket exclusion for knowledge including data room and public records | Delete; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Delete |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence of conditions before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Make CP. Require consent plus evidence |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3) | Release provided post-Completion | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective releases. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Require payout at Completion |
| Bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) | AUD 420k excluded from funds flow, "a matter for the Seller" | Specific line item or Seller-funded, including triggered on-costs | Add to funds flow; Seller to fund with on-costs |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 AUD 180k; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified either way | Broaden indemnity; require verification |
| Privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Investigate; preserve logs; require updates; assume neither confirmed breach nor loss in either direction | Reject materiality characterisation; require investigation terms |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | "Ordinary-course" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Assess; do not accept characterisation |
| Tax/IP (Seller update) | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Reject. Separate regime, still open |
| Title (DL 10) | DD-012 share register evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is internal only | Require independent evidence |

## Key reasoning

**1. Caps, thresholds and time limits.** Taken together, the Seller's terms would leave us with little recourse. The AUD 250,000 basket is an excess-only deductible, so we would bear the first AUD 250,000 of general claims and the basket would be five times ours. The AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude more small claims. The 18-month period would cut our window to general warranties, which may not surface until the first audit or tax cycle. The Seller's description of these as "market" means nothing against our approved positions.

**2. Fundamental/Title regime.** Treating title and capacity under the general caps and time limits is the most serious departure. Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason. Title must sit in its own regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

**3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** DL 1.1 deems every fact in the data room disclosed. Combined with cl 8.3, this would mean we have no claim for anything in our own data room, including the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and privacy issues already flagged. Together these clauses would undo most of our warranty protection. They must be struck.

**4. Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's draft applies the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" with no fraud exception. This is non-negotiable under the playbook and cannot be waived. It needs an express carve-out, not just a general reference.

**5. Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** DL 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met. "Consent on delivery" and "reasonable endeavours" would let us complete without the consent. We need the effective consent, evidence that its conditions are satisfied, and a Completion condition. We should also review cl 11.2 and 11.3 ourselves; the Seller's summary does not state the conditions.

**6. Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m outstanding).** DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included. The deal is debt-free/cash-free, so this should be discharged from Seller proceeds at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. The "approximately" figure needs a current payout letter.

**7. Bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs).** The funds flow excludes these amounts, and DL 5 does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation applies. The playbook requires a specific line item or Seller funding, including on-costs. Silent exclusion would shift a Seller obligation onto us through the purchase price, or onto the business post-Completion. We should confirm whether the bonuses are triggered by Completion itself and who pays the employer costs.

**8. Ironquay (AUD 180k).** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and does not address IP title or transfer. DL 4 says transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180k is not independently verified, so we should not treat it as the full exposure or as wrong. We should broaden the indemnity to cover transfer and title defects and third-party claims, preserve the Seller's cure right on SOW3, and require a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.

**9. Privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records).** The Seller calls this "not expected to be material," but DL 6 says it is unresolved: we do not know whether there was unauthorised access, the scope, or whether notification is required. Under the playbook we should neither assert a breach nor assume it is immaterial. We should require log preservation, an investigation timetable, regular updates, and disclosure of what the investigation has found. Given the personal information involved, we should ask privacy counsel whether any notification obligations could be triggered. Whether we need a specific indemnity or price holdback is a judgment call for Amelia Frost; the playbook does not decide it.

**10. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k).** "Ordinary-course" is a characterisation, not evidence. DL 8 says nothing about whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. We should assess the contracts and not automatically treat them as debt or deduct from price.

**11. Title.** The DD-012 share register is a Seller-supplied internal record. It is not independent proof of title, encumbrances or authority. We should require an ASIC extract, a PPSR search, transfer documents, and board and shareholder approvals.

**12. Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not. Our position is open, so we should not accept any unlimited-liability assumption or resolution.

**13. Lease and Mossvale consents (DL 7 and 9).** The Seller's disclosure leaves open whether the landlord or Mossvale must consent to the share sale. We should get legal confirmation and, if consent is required, make it a Completion condition. The playbook does not cover these directly.

## Recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Reject the package as a base document.** Respond that the Seller's "FINAL" and "[STANDARD]" labels are not accepted, and that all clauses are under review against Wattlebridge's positions.
2. **Confirm authority with Amelia Frost in writing** that no one has indicated acceptance of the 20% cap, 18-month period, or any other departure. Do not concede any fallback without her written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Restore the general regime:** 25%/AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24-month period, with the limits applying only to general warranties.
4. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Add a non-waivable fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate-misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
6. **Strike the data-room and public-register deemed disclosure** (DL 1.1, 1.2) and require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Delete the buyer-knowledge exclusion** (cl 8.3).
8. **Bluefen:** make effective consent and evidence of the cl 11.3 conditions a Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
9. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Funds flow:** add the AUD 420k bonuses as a specific line item or make them Seller-funded, including all on-costs. Do not allow silent exclusion.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, keep the SOW3 cure, require a confirmatory assignment, and seek verification of the AUD 180k.
12. **Privacy incident:** require log preservation, an investigation timetable and updates. Reject the "not material" characterisation. Obtain privacy counsel advice on notification. Decide with Amelia Frost whether a specific indemnity or holdback is needed.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the renewal terms. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
14. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.
15. **Tax and IP:** keep open, separate from the general regime, with no unlimited-liability assumption.
16. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm whether consents are required. If so, make them Completion conditions.
17. **Check clause references.** Several Seller cross-references (e.g. cl 3/6.3 for Bluefen, cl 2/7 for Riverlark) do not match the disclosure letter. Verify against the full SPA draft before responding.

Before anything goes to the Seller, a qualified NSW lawyer should review the mark-up, particularly the privacy notification question and the Fundamental/Title drafting.
=== END ADVICE ===
